preconditions.description: The number of nodes n and edges m are positive integers.

preconditions.expression: all(1 <= u <= n and 1 <= v <= n for u, v in edges)
preconditions.description: All edge endpoints are valid node indices between 1 and n.
The graph formed by n nodes and the given edges is connected.

postconditions.expression: len(result_nodes) == n and set(result_nodes) == set(range(1, n + 1))
postconditions.description: The output sequence contains exactly n distinct integers, forming a permutation of 1 to n.
The sequence starts with node 1, as Bob begins his wander there.

postconditions.expression: all(any(result_nodes[i] == u and result_nodes[i+1] == v or result_nodes[i] == v and result_nodes[i+1] == u for i in range(len(result_nodes)-1)) for u, v in edges)
postconditions.description: This clause is logically insufficient to capture the traversal constraint directly in a simple boolean without defining the path. Instead, we define the semantic property: The sequence represents a valid traversal where each new node is adjacent to the current position in the walk. However, the core requirement is lexicographical minimality among all valid DFS-like traversals.

The sequence result_nodes is the lexicographically smallest among all sequences generated by a valid wandering process starting at 1, where a valid process records a node only upon first visit and stops when all nodes are visited.
